newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin says voter polls distort campaign.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin says voter polls distort campaign.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin complained on Friday that voters were being misled by opinion polls in the media projecting the number of seats that each party would win in May 25-June 1 parliamentary elections.

"This type of presentation does not enable the French people to clearly measure the gap which exists today between one side and the other," said the opposition leader, whose party is lagging in the polls behind the current centre-right majority.
French polling firms' voter surveys in the weeks running up to the election ask voters to say which party they will be voting for in the first round.

The pollsters then use statistical models and past voting behaviour to translate voter preference into projections of how many seats each party will win after the second run-off round of voting has been completed.

Jospin said that France's two-round election system, in which one deputy will be elected from each of France's 577 constituencies, is too complex to project accurately seat breakdowns based on voter preference alone.
"The percentages given each political party in the first round describe, within the poll's margin of error, how the French people intend to vote.

"But calculations of the number of seats to be won in the second round are hypothetical, based on mathematical models and political projections which are simply not as precise," he said in a speech to party officials.
